after.focus: Dress a chopped bean salad without diluting it with draining water
after.outcome: Beans remain mostly intact, vegetables are crisp and pesto coats the ingredients instead of collecting in a watery pool.
before: Wash and dry vegetables. Drain and rinse the beans, then drain thoroughly; drain mozzarella from its packing liquid.
Use a bowl large enough to lift and fold a pint of tomatoes, a whole cucumber, beans and cheese without spilling. Larger batches need more mixing room.
Use ready-to-eat prepared pesto. Pesto often contains nuts and dairy; check its ingredients when serving someone with an allergy.

checkpoints.cue: Beans and mozzarella no longer drip freely before going into the bowl.
checkpoints.why: Packing or rinse liquid otherwise thins the measured dressing.

checkpoints.cue: Pesto reaches the beans and vegetables with only gentle folding.
checkpoints.why: Thorough distribution need not crush the tender beans.

troubleshooting.problem: Liquid gathers in the serving bowl
troubleshooting.cause: Wet ingredients and salted vegetables release water.
troubleshooting.fix: Drain the ingredients well next time. For this batch, use a slotted serving spoon and stir gently; adding more salt will not fix the water.

troubleshooting.cause: The salad was stirred forcefully or very soft beans were used.
troubleshooting.fix: Fold from the bottom with a broad spoon; broken beans cannot be made whole again.

substitutions.alternative: The same stated can size of drained/rinsed Great Northern beans
substitutions.effect: Great Northern beans have a slightly different texture; use the same stated can size and drain them thoroughly.

after.timing: About 15 minutes chopping/draining/mixing plus 10 minutes standing give 25 minutes elapsed. Standing time can be refrigerated. The finished volume depends on the size of the cucumber and how thoroughly the beans and cheese are drained.
after.storage: Keep at 40°F / 4°C or below and refrigerate within 2 hours total out of refrigeration, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Keep covered and use within 2 days. Texture softens and more liquid may collect. A salty pesto dressing does not make this cheese-and-vegetable salad shelf-stable.

## Chef's Note

Cannellini beans and mozzarella make this chopped cucumber-and-tomato salad substantial. Drain the beans and pat off excess water before tossing; pesto and red-wine vinegar form the dressing.

## Directions

1. **Continue:** Gently toss everything together in a large bowl and let sit for at least 10 minutes before serving.

2. **Continue:** This salad will keep well in the refrigerator, too!
changedFields.after:
## Chef's Note

Drain the cannellini beans and mozzarella well and dry the chopped vegetables so water does not dilute the pesto dressing. Fold gently to keep the beans intact, then allow ten minutes before serving. Pesto and cheese already contribute salt, so taste the fully mixed salad before any extra seasoning.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Wash and dry tomatoes and cucumber. Halve tomatoes, peel and dice cucumber, drain and halve mozzarella, and thinly slice shallot. Drain and rinse cannellini beans and let excess water drain away. Combine these ingredients in a large bowl.

2. **Dress:** Add the measured pesto, red wine vinegar, kosher salt and pepper.

3. **Fold and rest:** Fold gently until the dressing reaches all the ingredients. Let stand 10 minutes before serving, or refrigerate for that interval if preparing ahead.

4. **Serve or store:** Taste only after the dressing is fully distributed; add extra seasoning only if needed. Serve using clean utensils and refrigerate the unused salad promptly.
